title: Common Cryptography Patterns (Assessment Quick Reference)
description: Classical ciphers, encodings, and common mathematical pitfalls
detail:
1. Encoding chains: base16/32/58/62/64/85, hex, URL, uu; Chinese text → utf8/gbk hex
2. Classical: Caesar/Vigenère (quipqiup), rail fence, Bacon, Pigpen, keyboard coordinates, musical notation/Morse
3. RSA patterns: e=1/small e (cube-root attack), common modulus, small n (factor with yafu), same n with common factors, Wiener's/Boneh-Durfee (large e), high-bit p leak (Coppersmith), leaked dp/dq
4. Classical tools: start with RsaCtfTool, -n -e --decrypt
5. Hashes: length extension (hashpumpy); MD5 collision (fastcoll)
6. XOR: recover a repeating key byte by byte from known plaintext prefixes (e.g., flag{)
7. Elliptic curves: Smart's attack (anomalous curve)
8. LFSR/lattices: use sage for lattice methods; if sage is unavailable on the assessment CVM, use Python LLL implementations
In penetration assessments, crypto tasks are often small "decode to obtain credentials/proof artifacts" problems — focus on identification rather than deep derivation.
